crossRefs.note: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk?’
But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, answered them, “Why are you reasoning so in your hearts?
Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”

parallels.note: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk?’
Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you;’ or to say, ‘Arise and walk?’
He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.”

translations.web: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk?’
translations.bsb: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
translations.kjv: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?
translations.asv: Which is easier, to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins are forgiven; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?
